title: Get with a local
header_line: My analysis of one book on an entrepreneur's life. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Which country or market would you enter only with a local at your side?

I said that it is the first time I see the person in the book cede control. The man goes through the slide deck of maps, financing commitments and deal terms, and the person doesn't check the details. He asks: do you believe this is the right thing? I said it is the first time I see him fully reading another person and trusting their judgment.
A student said: he had a clear understanding of why he needed someone of that nature. Penetrating another country's culture is not an easy task.

A student who had consulted for a friend with a business in education said that, in their experience, some people don't even like to touch the subject of business until they have met you five, six, nine times. They really want to get to know you first.

I said I lived in the city, as a representative of a government, and that the joint venture was an incredible feat. In that country, I said, you do business their way or it's the highway. There is no negotiation. I said the book says half the cars were soon made there.
What do you do to mitigate risks in a foreign jurisdiction when you don't know your way around? A student said: partner with people who are comfortable in that jurisdiction.

I said that with my children everything becomes metaphorical. When they surf a new wave, I tell them: you cannot surf that break without a local, because you are missing information that could be detrimental to you. You could die.

Wherever I go, my number one rule is get with a local right away, I said. And you judge the local: do they have the resources to navigate the waters I want to navigate? Are they culturally aware? What is their status in that society?

I told of an exercise I gave a mentoree who wanted to go into politics: here is the number of a taxi driver in a city. You have one week to network through that driver to a senator and have lunch, on any topic. You will have to read about the country and map out how that relationship takes you to the top.
Who is the local you would trust, and how would you judge them?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write a market you want to enter.
Write who knows it and has the resources.
Write how you would judge them.
Write the one-week exercise you would set yourself.
Write the risks you are not yet aware of.

check.q: What did I say is my number one rule in a new place?
choices: Get with a local right away

check.q: What did the person in the book ask the man he trusted?
choices: Do you believe this is the right thing?

check.q: What did a student say about doing business in some places?
choices: People may want to know you first, over many meetings

recap: Get with a local and judge them well. Trust someone who knows, after you have checked.
